open_points.subject: A08 rule 6 vs A09 rule 6 outcome detail for stale/non-invocable bindings
open_points.text: A08 rule 6: "...nothing is sent and the element concludes `operation_failed` with detail `binding_stale` (A09 rule 6)." / A09 rule 6: "...The element concludes `operation_failed` with a detail naming the check..."
open_points.question: When pre-send checks fail because the binding/manifest is stale or no longer invocable, must the detail always be `binding_stale`, or must it name the specific failed check?
options: Always return `binding_stale` for all A08-rule-6 failures
Return specific check names (for example missing record, non-invocable route, digest mismatch)
Use `binding_stale` only for digest mismatch and specific names otherwise
open_points.default_guess: Always return `binding_stale` for any A08-rule-6 failure.

open_points.subject: A08 rule 6 re-check scope at send time
open_points.text: "fails one of rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own"
open_points.question: Exactly which rule-5 checks are considered "of the record itself" during invocation re-check, especially checks that also depend on binding ports (idempotency-key fields and request-shape fit)?
options: All non-instance checks from rule 5, including key-field and request-shape compatibility against the binding
A fixed subset to be listed explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Apply all rule-5 checks except instance-selection/header checks.

open_points.subject: A14 resume ordering by `map_index`
open_points.text: "Resume ... sends again, in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order — an element without `map_index` before index 0"
open_points.question: What exact ordering must be used for `map_index` values (numeric ascending, lexical, or store order)?
options: Numeric ascending integer order, with no-index first
Unicode lexical order on serialized index, with no-index first
open_points.default_guess: Numeric ascending order with no-index first.

open_points.subject: A10 approval coverage when request metadata changes
open_points.text: "...equal digests mean the same request, provided the instance's `api_base_url` is still the one the preview showed; after a restart that changed it, the approval no longer covers the send..."
open_points.question: If other request-forming metadata changes after restart (required headers, credential header name/value, instance class/TLS allowance), does an existing approval still cover the send?
options: Any change in effective HTTP request metadata invalidates approval
Approval always remains valid as long as input digests match
open_points.default_guess: Any change to effective request metadata should require a fresh approval.

open_points.subject: Unknown effect attempts when run ends `refused`/`failed`
open_points.text: A10 rule 3: "Refusing writes one NodeExecution `refused_by_owner` ... and ends the run `refused`..." and A11 rule 5 only specifies: "Cancelling a run whose element waits on an unknown outcome leaves that EffectAttempt `unknown`"
open_points.question: If a run ends `refused` or `failed` while another element already has an `unknown` EffectAttempt, what final handling is required for that attempt?
options: Leave it `unknown` permanently; no further resolution allowed because run ended
open_points.default_guess: Leave it `unknown` and non-resolvable once the run has ended.

open_points.subject: A01 purpose-check precedence vs A16 request-check order
open_points.text: A01 rule 5: "This check comes before every other check of the request." / A16 rule 1: request checks are ordered as size -> token/config -> operation/schema -> actor -> operation-specific checks.
open_points.question: Does the slot/flow purpose-consistency check run literally before all checks (including schema/token), or only before other operation-specific checks?
options: Run purpose check only within operation-specific checks (after A16 global checks)
Run purpose check before any other validation including schema/actor checks
open_points.default_guess: A16 global gateway checks run first; A01 purpose check runs first within operation-specific checks.
